Unlike sibling methods that suffer from blurring or deformation errors over long sequences, ReRF maintains high photorealism and sharpness regardless of frame count by using a keyframe-based residual compression strategy [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'INGP-T and TiNeuVox suffer from severe blurring effects as the frame count increases' and that 'DeVRF... is difficult when motion is large in long sequences.' It further claims that 'no matter how the number of frames increases... our method always maintains high photorealism and sharpness.' Additionally, the evidence describes the method as using a 'keyframe-based strategy' where the sequence is divided into Groups Of Feature grids (GOFs) starting with an I-feature grid (keyframe) followed by P-feature grids (residuals), which aligns with the 'keyframe-based residual compression strategy' mentioned in the claim.
